column1: What is happening in the North-West?
column2: Sokoto–Badagry Superhighway, Abuja–Kaduna–Kano road Section II (₦304bn), Kano–Maradi rail ($1.3bn) and Kaduna–Kano rail. The zone had the largest share (₦5.97tn) of federal project approvals in 2025.
column3: Faster movement of grain, livestock and goods to market.

column1: What is happening in the North-East?
column2: About ₦1.5tn of NEDC projects, 70,000 solar streetlights (2024–25), the Akwanga–Jos–Bauchi–Gombe–Biu–Maiduguri road corridor and Dadin Kowa hydropower.
column3: Rebuilding communities and reconnecting markets after years of insurgency.

column1: What is happening in the North-Central and the FCT?
column2: Abuja light rail back in service, the Trans-Sahara Superhighway (₦489bn), Gurara hydropower, the 3,112-unit Karsana housing project and the Gora solar park in Nasarawa.
column3: Better transport, power and housing for the middle belt.

column1: What is happening in the South-West?
column2: The western sections of the Lagos–Calabar Coastal Highway, the Badagry end of the Sokoto–Badagry Superhighway, Lagos–Ibadan corridor works and busier ports.
column3: Faster freight to ports and factories, and jobs in construction and logistics.

column1: What is happening in the South-East?
column2: Enugu–Onitsha Expressway, Second Niger Bridge access roads, the Enugu–Abakaliki corridor, Port Harcourt–Aba rail and the new South-East Development Commission.
column3: Lower freight costs for South-East traders and manufacturers.

column1: What is happening in the South-South?
column2: Lagos–Calabar Coastal Highway, Bodo–Bonny road and bridges, East–West Road works, zero piracy in 2025 and oil revenue now paid directly into the Federation Account.
column3: Opening up the Niger Delta's coast to trade, tourism and investment.
